name: Prime
description: One word at a time, white Difference-blend captions (each letter shows the negative of the footage behind it), a heavy tight lowercase grotesk for most words and a large swash formal script for the payoff word of each line. Reproduced from Toby de Boer's reel (analysis/reference_spec.json). Font paths are relative to this file; sizes are fractions of frame height; em values are relative to the layout's sans font size.

reference.source: Instagram reel by Toby de Boer (@tobydeboer), 1916x1078, 24 fps, 6.8 s

render.blend_space: display-referred sRGB (like After Effects 8/16 bpc and CSS mix-blend-mode)

sans.note: Stand-in for Helvetica Now Display Bold / Neue Haas Display 75. ss07 gives the square i/j dots of the reference. Tracking -0.075 em = AE tracking -75. word_space_em widens spaces so 'but i' / 'in the' keep the reference's ~0.18 em word gap despite the tight tracking.

script.note: Stand-in for Kuenstler Script / a heavy-shaded roundhand. Lowercase from Pinyon Script at 2.2 x the sans size (x-height ~1.6x the sans x-height); the swash capital is drawn from Imperial Script at 2.9x the lowercase x-height, about 3x the sans ascender like the reference (Prime/They 3.4, Win 3.1, Regardless 2.7). stem_boost thickens only the shaded stems.

stem_boost.note: Heavier shaded downstrokes, hairlines untouched: strokes at least open_em wide are grown by grow_em (total width, em of the script size). Brings Pinyon's stems toward the reference's 18 px stems at an 83 px x-height without clogging the hairlines the way a uniform stroke_em does.

difference.note: default: out = |1 - B| inside the letters

difference_pink.note: 'at my Prime': difference with a pink fill, out = |C - B| (fitted C = 0.886, 0.545, 0.545)

normal.note: 'Win' / 'but i': plain opaque white for a bright, celebratory shot

blur_in.note: 'They' f086-f093: opacity rises while an extra Gaussian blur shrinks to 0 (curves sampled evenly over duration_s; blur sigma in sans em)

glitch.note: What reads as a 'glitch' in the reference (f001-f008, f060, f100) is NOT an RGB split (measured channel offsets < 0.5 px): it is the footage running on 2s (held frame pairs) while the difference letters invert moving lights. So for Prime the glitch entrance only holds footage frames in pairs; RGB split and slice displacement are supported but set to 0.

glitch_rgb.note: Optional digital glitch for A/B tests (NOT in the reference): small channel split + horizontal slice shifts of the letters for ~3 frames, decaying to 0. Use on the opening word only.

timing.note: A caption shows from its start frame until the next caption starts (no gaps, no overlaps, as in the reference). If the pause before the next caption is longer than max_gap_s, it leaves tail_after_end_s (+ emphasis_extra_hold_s for script words) after its spoken end and the screen is empty. A first caption that starts within first_unit_lead_in_s is pulled to frame 0. A caption squeezed below min_flash_s by the next one starts up to a few frames early, taking them from its predecessor (which keeps min_hold_s).

zoom.note: The captions are composited first and the digital zoom is applied to the composite about the frame centre, so the text scales with the footage (measured to 0.2%). Each event eases exponentially from the current scale: s(t) = s0 + (to - s0)(1 - exp(-(t - t0)/tau)). Script words punch in +11..13% (tau ~4 frames at 24 fps); the word after a punch settles back.

subject_mask.note: Opt-in depth variant: behind_subject captions are multiplied by (1 - matte) so the person occludes them. The reference never occludes anything, so plans leave behind_subject off unless asked (plan_rules.variants.behind_subject.enabled). Matte = thresholded mask, eroded erode_px, edge decided by the footage's luma (edge_luma_gate), feathered feather_px.

edge_luma_gate.note: Inside a band_px rim of the (eroded) mask only pixels brighter than the dark sky count as subject, so the hair itself decides the edge (segmentation masks sit 3-12 px proud of the hair).

montage.description: Reference layout: 16:9 montage, every caption centred in the frame.

stack.note: 'They / don't / wanna': left-anchored block, don't left-aligned to the swash, wanna centred under They, very tight leading, staggered blur-ins, all three cut out together.

talking_head.description: Vertical selfie talking head. Default = the reference's own layout: words centred, ascender-to-baseline box on the frame's middle (sans baseline 0.515 H, script baseline 0.53 H), which on a centred face lands on the forehead/hairline above the eyes, where the lit skin and hair move behind the letters. 'chin' is the fallback for clips where H/2 falls on the eyes; 'top_of_head' is the opt-in depth test. Every caption's zoomed ink box is kept inside safe_zone (bottom 0.75 H clears the Reels username/caption/audio UI).

default.note: Reference layout (ascender-to-baseline box ~centred on H/2); 0.515 rather than 0.524 so j/g descenders clear the eyes.

chin.note: Fallback for clips where the frame middle falls on the eyes: across the chin / collar (the safe zone clamps it above 0.75 H).

top_of_head.note: Opt-in depth test (with behind_subject): baseline = median top of the subject mask over the word's frames + y_offset, so only the baseline zone of the letters tucks behind the hair.

safe_zone.note: Fractions of the frame; enforced after the digital zoom (max zoom over the caption's frames). Words that would cross it are shrunk (width) or moved (height).

emphasis.note: Script = the payoff content word that completes a line (noun, number word, strong verb, final adverb), ~1 in 5-6 words, never function words, never adjacent, and always the last word. Auto-pick ranks content words by spoken duration x length.

grouping.note: Only runs of function words are grouped (right-to-left pairs: 'at my', 'at a', 'in the', 'but i'). A caption shorter than min_unit_s joins a neighbouring function-word caption; content words are never merged (merge_content_words false), so a lone function word next to content words stands alone if it lasts at least min_unit_s_alone (the reference shows 'i'm' for 2 frames).

behind_subject.note: Off by default (the reference never occludes). build_plan.py --behind WORD or enabled=true turns the depth test on.

sync.note: Whisper sometimes stretches a word back over a pause. If a word's whisper span starts in silence (speech-band energy below floor + voiced_db_above_floor for min_voiced_s) and the first voiced onset is more than min_shift_s later, the caption starts at that onset minus lead_s (text leading the sound by a frame reads as in sync). min_shift_s 0.15 ignores the 50-100 ms unvoiced bursts of k/t/p onsets. skip_first: the opening caption is pulled to frame 0 anyway (timing.first_unit_lead_in_s), as the reference opens on a caption at f001.
